evidence: Cic. Att. 12.37.1: Pīliam et Atticam plānē bellē sē habēre
terms.comment: With an adverb: bene, male, melius mē habeō. For “feel” with an adjective Latin mostly uses esse: fessus sum, I feel tired.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.8.1: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō
terms.comment: Minus valeō, I’m not so well; melius valeō, I feel better. Cicero’s letters open Sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō.

phrases.latin: ut prīmum gravitātem urbis excessī et illum odōrem culīnārum fūmantium … prōtinus mūtātam valētūdinem sēnsī
phrases.english: as soon as I had left the heavy air of the city and that smell of smoking kitchens … I felt better at once

phrases.latin: sī valēs, bene est, ego valeō. valētūdinem tuam velim cūrēs dīligentissimē.
phrases.english: If you are well, good; I am well. Please take the greatest care of your health.

sources: Lewis & Short: habeo · Lewis & Short: valeo
